regime: Trend-Up Reclaim (Risk-On Rotation, Vol Back to the Lows)
summary: The bounce turned into a reclaim. NQ added a second up day, tagging 30,114 and closing near the 30,000 round at 30,023, while MES closed 7,800, both back above their EMA50 and ATR stops. Gold lagged at 4,159 under its stop and crude faded to 97.72 below its own, while VIX fell to 16.68, back to the mid-month lows. The catch: the overnight has already reversed hard and handed most of Wednesday back, so the reclaim is unconfirmed.

risk.sizing: Reduced, reclaim unconfirmed after the overnight reversal
risk.openRisk: NQ and MES trend-longs are on above their stops and EMA50, but the overnight reversed and both gold and crude are below their stops, so the reclaim is unconfirmed.
risk.note: Throttle state REDUCED. No drawdown flags, daily loss budget unused, sizing stays trimmed. Wednesday earned a cleaner read, with NQ and MES both back above their stops and EMA50 for a second day, but the overnight already reversed and handed most of it back, so the reclaim is unconfirmed and this is not the spot to add. Keep size reduced until Thursday's RTH holds above the stops (MNQ 29,779, MES 7,765) and reclaims EMA50 (MNQ 29,861, MES 7,770). Gold is still below its stop and mean, so the safe-haven long stays off until it reclaims 4,161. Crude lost its December stop and faded from the 100 area, so the trend-long is off until it reclaims 98.93, and mind the roll with January now on MCL2!. VIX back at 16.68 is calm, which cuts both ways, less fear but also less of the volatility the momentum edge needs. The data calendar stays thin with the shutdown backdrop, so treat any headline as the catalyst. Next policy event is the FOMC meeting Oct 27 to 28.

psychology: Two green days in a row feel like permission to size up. Slow down. The reclaim is real on the daily close, but the overnight just showed how fast price can hand it back. The habit that pays is separating what the chart did from what you want it to do next. A confirmed reclaim is one you can still see on the chart the next morning. If it already failed before the open, it was never confirmed in the first place. Let price hold the level for a session before you trust it, and keep your risk the same size on day two of a move as it was on day one.
